newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville says peak loads cut surplus for Friday.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville says peak loads cut surplus for Friday.

text.p: High demand due to colder weather in the Pacific Northwest eliminated surplus power available for Friday pre-schedulings, Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) trade sources said Thursday.
But they also acknowledged failure to sell very much of the 300 megawatts (MW) of firm peak power offered on Wednesday for Thursday delivery.
BPA had raised prices for Thursday by $3.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) to $16.00 for Northwest sales and $17.00 for California-Oregon border (COB).
"It's a good thing we didn't sell it all, because we needed some extra for our own loads this morning," one BPA trader said.
He said the agency would "definitely" have surplus peak power for Sunday and probably Saturday, but Monday's offers will depend on the weather.
The Northwest is expected to see temperatures 2 to 8 degrees F below normal through early next week, according to Weather Services Corp.
